clue.text: A newspaper leader

parts.note: reads as the opinion column at the front of a paper, but means the person who heads the paper and writes that column

explanation.surface: A remark about the lead article in a daily paper.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'leader' in British papers is an opinion article; the person at the top of the paper writes it and also leads the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief journalist in charge of a paper is its head, its leader in the human sense.

clue.text: Women tend to make such provision

indicators.note: the two words are worked over to make something new, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Women are inclined to put something aside for the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' rearranges the letters of WOMEN TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift of money or property set aside to provide income is a form of provision for someone.

clue.text: Parking is interrupting the cricket perhaps — have a look

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the middle of the other, so the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: a cricket is an example of an insect, hence 'perhaps'
P is the map and road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A car park disrupting a cricket match invites someone to go and see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cricket' suggests the sport (a British bat-and-ball game), but it is the chirping creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something is to examine it closely, to look it over.

clue.text: Work on site can cause obstruction

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
a site is a position or location

explanation.surface: Building work on a plot of land can cause a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposition is resistance, something that blocks or hinders.

clue.text: Accommodation that's barred for fliers

parts.note: suggests a prison for airmen, but describes a home with bars for small feathered pets

explanation.surface: A secure lock-up for pilots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fliers' hints at aviators; the barred lodging is for birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage for a pet bird is a small barred home for creatures that fly.

clue.text: Grows wrinkled

definitions.meaning: read as two words, in folds or furrows, as a crumpled shirt is

explanation.surface: Something gets bigger and crinkled at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer as IN CREASES.
explanation.definitionFit: To get bigger is to expand; to be full of folds is to be creased all over, in two senses.

clue.text: A mild imprecation — here's an example

definitions.meaning: a gentle oath, as in an old-fashioned exclamation of annoyance
points at the printed punctuation mark just before it in the clue

explanation.surface: Someone gives an instance of a gentle swear word.
explanation.walkthrough: The long punctuation stroke in the clue is itself an instance of the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a polite curse ('Dash it!') and also the name of the punctuation stroke printed in the clue.

clue.text: Inclined to love having a pal round about four

indicators.note: the friend's word goes round the outside of the number, so it encloses it

parts.note: a mate is a pal, a friend
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone fond of romance has a friend nearby, at around four o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Amative is a formal word for amorous, disposed toward romance.

clue.text: A woman trains all individually

parts.note: Eve is a woman's name, the first woman in Genesis
RY is an abbreviation for railway, which runs trains

explanation.surface: A woman coaches everybody one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trains' looks like a verb (coaches) but is the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means each one without exception, taken one by one.

clue.text: Reverse for a French party .

parts.note: UN is French for 'a'
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A French party is called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverse an action is to cancel it out, as with the computer command.

clue.text: Stand up awkwardly or stoop down to use this

indicators.note: done clumsily, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Advice on posture: rise clumsily, or bend down to use a household item.
explanation.definitionFit: You crouch to the floor with a small shovel to sweep up dirt into it.

clue.text: No gentleman will go into action in a downpour

indicators.note: the rogue is placed inside the lawsuit, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a case is a legal action, a lawsuit
a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, no gentleman

explanation.surface: A rogue starts doing something during heavy rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' reads as activity, but here it is the legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a heavy fall of water, a torrent.

clue.text: New towns — these will give one the desired edge

definitions.text: will give one the desired edge

indicators.note: something new is a fresh version, so the letters of the two words are reshaped

explanation.surface: New towns are promoted as offering residents an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpening stones are used to put a keen blade on knives and tools.

clue.text: The most idyllic homes are neat inside

indicators.note: the phrase houses the answer within it, so the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: The most perfect houses are orderly within.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy means orderly, kept in good order.

clue.text: Not all put by a little money over a period

parts.note: per means by, as in 'per post'
a cent is a small coin
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone saves only part of a small sum of money over time.
explanation.definitionFit: A percentage is a proportion or share, a part rather than the whole.

clue.text: Accord the right style

definitions.meaning: to grant someone a right or claim
as a verb, to call by a name or title

explanation.surface: A command to give someone a proper manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is both to give a claim to something and to give a name or title.

clue.text: Removed without hesitation and made use of

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside: the cut-out word stands outside the pause

parts.note: excised means cut out, removed
ER is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Something was taken out decisively and then put to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or power is to use it.

clue.text: A woman gone to find a drinking-den

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
been as in 'has been to', has gone somewhere

explanation.surface: A woman leaves in search of an illicit bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed Irish or Scottish drinking house.

clue.text: Bedclothes?

parts.note: usually means sheets and blankets; the question mark invites reading it as clothes worn in bed

explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nighties are garments for bed, clothes for bed in a literal sense.

clue.text: The little toad!

parts.note: sounds like an insult to a naughty child, but means a young frog or toad before it grows legs

explanation.definitionFit: A pollywog is the larval stage of a toad, literally a little toad.

clue.text: Let down, so fed-up and behindhand

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'up' means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
late means behind time, behindhand

explanation.surface: Someone disappointed, being tired of waiting and running behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflate is to let the air out, to let it down like a tyre.

clue.text: Stuff for firing

explanation.surface: Material to feed a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse sack-cloth is a fabric, and getting the sack is dismissal.

clue.text: A Moslem — one rushed and in a tizzy

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
ran means rushed

indicators.note: a state of agitation, so the two short words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A Muslim man hurried along in a flap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tizzy' rearranges IN A to give IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Iran is most likely a follower of Islam (an old definition by example).

clue.text: As a result the foot is weak

parts.note: so means therefore, as a result
FT is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: Consequently someone's foot is feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft means lacking strength or firmness.

clue.text: Poles are distilling gin

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Polish people are making spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland, and 'gin' a drink; gin is also a trap for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a trap for catching game, the same as a snare.

clue.text: Article about foreign nobleman — a hard worker, he figures

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
C is short for circa, about
a count is a European noble
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about a European aristocrat says he toils hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A book-keeper works with numbers, so he figures in the sense of calculating.

clue.text: Remaining throughout

definitions.meaning: all through, as in 'all the world ...'

explanation.surface: Something persists from start to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Over means left behind as surplus, and also through every part.

clue.text: Note there are many on strike

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, a large number
to hit is to strike

explanation.surface: A message saying lots of workers are taking industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests a walkout but means a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A chit is a short written note or voucher.

clue.text: For American Indians, cheap as can be

indicators.note: the letters can be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Something is being sold to Native Americans at rock-bottom prices.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a group of Native American peoples of the south-western US.

clue.text: Look into cut-back by colliery

indicators.note: the word for cutting is turned back to front

parts.note: to axe is to cut
a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Investigate job cuts at the coal pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-back' looks like a single noun (a reduction) but splits into AXE turned 'back' to give EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to inspect or investigate it.

clue.text: There's a regular stream at day's end

parts.note: even means regular, steady
tide in its old sense of a current or stream

explanation.surface: A steady current flows by at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening.

clue.text: Persons enveloping a sovereign's letters are not so well-born

indicators.note: the people wrap around the letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: men are persons
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the monarch's initials

explanation.surface: People wrap up a letter from the Queen; they are lesser folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaner in its old sense means of lower birth or humbler rank.
